_meta.role: Senior Embedded Software Developer / Embedded Software Engineer (m/f/d) C/C++ & RTOS

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, writing embedded software in C and C++ on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers. Built bare-metal device drivers (GPIO, timers, ADC, I2C) within 3.68 KB Flash, FreeRTOS applications with mutex-protected tasks and interrupt-driven UART, and closed-loop control algorithms from encoder odometry, using Git, CMake and Linux.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers over I2C with a Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, converting 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback control.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a PyQt user interface for real-time laboratory data acquisition; used GitLab for version control and documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed ARM Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) within 3.68 KB Flash and 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C device driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Built FreeRTOS firmware on STM32 using mutexes for shared-memory task coordination, with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Drove multi-servo PWM control from detections streamed over UART; integrated VL53L0X time-of-flight sensing over I2C with OLED display.

projects.name: Robocon Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Implemented closed-loop heading correction from dual-axis quadrature encoder odometry (2400 CPR), feeding angular error back into rotation PWM to hold course during translation.
Wrote interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles as a 4-bit A/B state machine, drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM, and added a fail-safe halt on USB controller disconnect.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on the microcontroller, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection from dual VL53L0X sensors over a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer.
Built software interfaces between subsystems and the user interface over a WebSocket fabric; optimized runtime from 56.7 ms to 10.9 ms (5.2x) at 100% pick reliability.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
